- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently fails to adjust downward fast enough; delay peak forecast by 1–2 days and reduce amplitude.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 30-day moving average, model tends to overcorrect; align forecast toward historical mean or 30-day MA.
- For horizon > 14 days, model often underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.5% buffer for negative sentiment or volatility spikes.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., -0.3 → +0.2 → -0.4), model misreads momentum; reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% in such regimes.
